rulings.restated: Enter the amount from helper "Schedule SE line 13 (deduction for one-half of self-employment tax) for this person".
rulings.model: The Schedule SE that feeds this line takes line 2 from all of the person's Schedule C results with no exclusion. The SE instructions say "If you were a statutory employee, don't include the net profit or (loss) from Schedule C, line 31, on Schedule SE, line 2", and notary profit is likewise excluded. Neither case is screened or refused.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: refusal located elsewhere; restatement accepted. Statutory employee income and notary fees are refused on each Schedule C (the sc screens: 'statutory employee (box 13 of Form W-2 was checked), or fees you received as a notary public'; i1040sse p. 4), so every Schedule C result that reaches Schedule SE line 2 belongs there; church employee income and the other exclusions are refused through person.se_screen.

rulings.restated: Add w2.one over every confirmed w2 entry, within the current person when parent-bound. An unanswered roster is unknown.
rulings.model: The IRS condition is "had more than one employer for 2025", but the restatement counts confirmed W-2 entries. One employer can issue several Forms W-2, which would wrongly count as more than one employer.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; project retained. The W-2 collection is keyed by employer, and repeated forms from one employer are consolidated into one entry ("Keyed by employer within person; consolidate repeated forms for the same employer explicitly", forms/2025/w2.yaml collection note), so the count of entries is the count of employers that "had more than one employer for 2025" (i1040gi p. 117) asks for. No change to the data.

rulings.restated: Add w2.one over every confirmed w2 entry for which helper "Did this employer withhold more than $10,918.20?" = true, within the current person when parent-bound. An unanswered roster is unknown.
rulings.model: The IRS test is "if any one employer withheld more than $10,918.20", but the restatement tests each W-2 entry. The text does not establish that one W-2 entry equals one employer, and an employer issuing several W-2s could exceed the limit in total while no single entry does.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; project retained. The W-2 collection is keyed by employer, and repeated forms from one employer are consolidated into one entry ('Keyed by employer within person; consolidate repeated forms for the same employer explicitly', forms/2025/w2.yaml), so the count of entries over the limit is the count of employers over the limit.

rulings.restated: Add w2.wages over every confirmed w2 entry, within the current person when parent-bound. An unanswered roster is unknown.
rulings.model: The IRS text says only "total wages of more than $176,100" and does not say which W-2 box supplies those wages. The program's field w2.wages is not defined in the text given, so the operand cannot be verified.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; project retained. The $176,100 test is on social security wages, the wage base above which no social security tax is withheld (i1040gi p. 117, line 11; $10,918.20 is 6.2% of $176,100), so `w2.wages` sums Form W-2 box 3 (social security wages) and box 7 (social security tips), the amounts the tax was withheld on. No change to the data.
